newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast seeks tighter ACPC coffee output limit.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast seeks tighter ACPC coffee output limit.

text.p: Ivory Coast called on Monday for an emergency Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) council meeting to tighten a 1996/97 export limit programme and agree a response to increased exports by non-members.

Ivorian Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze opened the 36th general assembly of the Inter-African Coffee Organisation (IACO) noting the programme had been well supported, especially in Africa, but had had mixed results.
He blamed production and exports by non-members Mexico, Vietnam and Guatemala.

"Members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries and in particular those of the Inter-African Coffee Organisation must reassess the export limit programme and must adopt a more efficient marketing strategy," he said.

"We must strengthen the export limitation programme coupled with a 'prompt response strategy'," Gauze said, adding that IACO would formulate concrete technical proposals to put to ACPC allies such as Brazil, the world's top producer, and Colombia.
The 14-member ACPC accounts for over 80 percent of world production although a handful of medium-sized producer nations are not members.
World coffee prices, which slumped in the early 1990s, soared after frost in Brazil in 1994 but have since slid again.
The ACPC export programme limits members' green coffee exports to 53.5 million 60-kg bags in the year to June 1997 compared to 48.9 million in 1995/96.
The programme had succeeded in cutting stocks held by consumers to their lowest level for 20 years -- 480,000 tonnes.

"We have to recognise, however, that the second objective of raising world prices and stabilising them at remunerative levels is far from being achieved," Gauze said, adding that roasters had opted for a policy of buying only when they needed to.

He blamed non-members' exports for the fall in prices. "Mexico and Vietnam, producing nations that are not ACPC members, and Guatemala, recently intensified their exports, scorning rules proclaimed and adopted by ACPC member nations."

Gauze said current stocks held by consumers appeared too high given the new roasters' policy and called for urgent consultations between African producers and their partners in Latin America and Asia for an emergency meeting of the ACPC council to discuss two themes -
* review and adjustment of the ACPC 1996/97 export programme
* ACPC strategy towards non-members taking advantage of ACPC regulation efforts to boost their exports.
Ivory Coast, which produces robusta, is Africa's top exporter of coffee. The general assembly of the 25-member IACO ends on Wednesday.
